constructs its decl, and the constructed body IS the edge list, read

source order from the stmt list, never the demand order the worklist
drains in; and a module with no main seeds all decls rather than

mentl/949ac34:
The keyed ev-scan served two callers with one silent miss-path:
return 0. For the FORWARD side (LEvRef building a callee's pair from
this frame) a miss is routine — capture sets over-approximate, a
caller legitimately lacks keys its callee never fires. For the
PERFORM side, a miss — or a FOUND key whose entry is the 0 an
unfilled pair planted — meant record=load(0)/base=load(4): dispatch
through the int_to_str/iovec scratch words, calling whichever valid
table fn their bytes named at that instant. The blanket-trap
experiment measured the populations: ALL EIGHT rungs trap if
forwards go strict (misses are structural volume), so the split is
the form: ev_lookup stays tolerant; the new ev_perform_entry traps
at the read on sentinel-miss AND found-but-zero, writing the sought
key and base to the scratch postmortem window first. Both emitters
route performs through the strict form — wheel emit_ev_entry_perform
and the seed's $emit_ev_entry_perform, mirrored; LEvRef keeps the
tolerant read in both layers.

verify 35/35; the five integer rungs hold through the strict scan —
every bomb of the found-zero class is now defused loud, m2-wide.

And the measurement the split leaves behind: the pinned +rt misroute
(instantiate's mint performing wat_stdout's arm) does NOT fire the
new trap — the mint key's entry is VALID and WRONG. The corruption
is in the PLACEMENT: one region-write up the forward chain filled
the right key with a foreign handler's entry. The seam's next dig is
one probe wide: dump the region bytes at the break.

mentl/94a331f:
Adds wasi_fs.wat — WAT-layer transcription of the FX walkthrough's
filesystem effect substrate. Provides path-relative-to-fd primitives
that the compiled wheel's `wasi_filesystem` handler arms call into.
Composes with the existing FX.A.basics (`d801511`) + FX.B (`afc4b0c`)
substrate already in lib/runtime/io.nx + src/mentl_voice.nx
mentl_voice_filesystem handler.

Architecture:
  - 5 new WASI preview1 imports added to Layer 0 shell in build.sh:
      path_create_directory, path_filestat_get, path_unlink_file,
      path_rename, fd_readdir
  - $wasi_fs_cwd_fd_g global defaults to 3 (wasmtime convention:
    --dir=. preopens fd 3 = "."). Caller can override via
    $fs_set_cwd_fd if running under a different invocation.
  - All operations return WASI errno (i32, 0 = success); callers
    surface errno via the wasi_filesystem handler arm's diagnostic
    chain per FX walkthrough.

Exports (7 functions):
  CWD config:
    $fs_set_cwd_fd, $fs_get_cwd_fd
  Path operations:
    $fs_create_directory(path) — path_create_directory wrapper
    $fs_unlink(path) — path_unlink_file (file removal; not dirs)
    $fs_rename(old, new) — atomic rename within cwd
    $fs_filestat_is_dir(path) — returns 1 iff path exists + is dir
                                (filetype = WASI_FILETYPE_DIRECTORY = 3
                                 at offset 16 of filestat record)
  Directory listing:
    $fs_list_dir(path) — opens path as dir + reads dirents into a
                         4096-byte buffer + parses name-length-
                         prefixed entries (24-byte header + name +
                         8-byte alignment padding) + returns flat
                         list of name strings.

mentl/940a626:
Extends docs/SYNTAX.md §Comments §Doc comments with the canonical
substrate doctrine for `///`. Replaces the prior minimal subsection
with the full positive-form spec.

Doctrine:

- `///` is the developer's one voice into the substrate. Lexer emits
  TDocComment(text); parser attaches via Documented(content, stmt)
  AST wrapper per DS §3.1+§3.2; inference threads as
  DocstringReason(content, span) per DS §3.1 candidate C; Mentl
  surfaces verbatim alongside her canonical projection per MV §2.7
  + F.1 §3.1, §5.

What `///` IS:
- Pure prose; multi-line concatenates per DS §5 AT-DS3
- Attaches to immediately-following decl; module-level attaches to
  synthetic Module handle per F.1 §3.2
- Surfaces verbatim — Mentl has no semantic parse; render handlers
  interpret presentation per target (HTML / terminal / markdown)
- Lede + body structure (RTerse shows lede; RExplain shows full)
- Cross-references via backticks resolved by render handlers
- Code blocks compile via the same pipeline; no doc-tests as
  separate category per INSIGHTS L398

What `///` is NOT:
- Not a markup language (no `=== headers ===`, no `// ─── name ───`)
- Not JSDoc/JavaDoc/Sphinx tags (no @param/@returns/@throws/@since/
  @deprecated/:func:/:type:); effect row + refinement carry that;
  positive-form discipline forbids lifecycle vocabulary
- Not gated by docstring content; Mentl unsilenceable per MV §2.7.5
- Not the only voice; substrate-derived Mentl is the second voice;
  no editorial third per F.1 §5

Relationship to `//`:
- `//` silently consumed by lexer; no graph presence; no Mentl presence
- Use for implementation notes inside fn bodies / file-skim markers
- The choice IS "human-only context" vs "substrate the medium reads"

Citations: DS-docstring-edge.md (substrate), F1-inka-doc.md §3.1+§5
(projection), MV-mentl-voice.md §2.7 (surfacing), INSIGHTS L398
(no doc-tests), CLAUDE.md (positive-form discipline).

mentl/944f443:
Mode-11 pattern `\+\+\s*\[[^\]]*\]` was matching `[t]` but not
`[elem]` under GNU grep 3.12 ERE. The escaped `\]` inside the
negated character class parses inconsistently — `[^\]]` fails to
match multi-char content followed by `]`.

Fix: drop the backslash escape inside the class. `[^]]*` correctly
means "zero or more characters that aren't `]`" in ERE.
